elements.element: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with a minimum limit of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 contains no commercial general liability insurance requirement.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with a minimum aggregate limit of USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 contains no commercial general liability insurance requirement or aggregate limit.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 requires professional liability insurance of only USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor shall maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative language requires only USD 2,000,000. It does not provide the required USD 5,000,000 coverage, and the Customer Data processing condition is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 contains no workers' compensation insurance requirement.

elements.element: Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer upon Customer's request.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 contains no certificate-of-insurance delivery obligation.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 requires Commerce One to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause 14.11 requires Commerce One to maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

result.reason: The added operative provision exactly reaches the fallback coverage types and limits without adding unrelated requirements. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits commercial general liability, workers' compensation, and certificates on request, and its E&O and cyber/privacy limits are below the preferred amounts. The amendment preserves the existing commercial terms, although placing the new clause after the execution recital is structurally awkward.
